issues.description: The solution repository implements animal classes with names SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat, while the problem statement and the template expect Seal, Pig, and Goat. The problem text and UML explicitly ask students to implement classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (and the template Main instantiates Seal, Pig, Goat). In the solution the corresponding Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java files are empty and the working implementations are provided under different identifiers (SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat). This identifier mismatch makes it unclear which class names students should use and may confuse mapping between the specification, template usage, and the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent across artifacts. Either (a) rename SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, and Goat in the solution (or provide implemented Seal/Pig/Goat classes that delegate to the Space* implementations), or (b) update the problem statement and template to refer to the Space* class names. Ensure the solution contains non-empty implementations for the exact class names used in the specification and template so students can map requirements to concrete classes.
